name: CORS Configuration
description: Enforces proper CORS setup for APIs with explicit origins, methods, and credential handling.
content:
# CORS Configuration Rules

- Never use `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with credentials — browsers reject it and it signals a misconfiguration
- Explicitly list allowed origins — `['https://app.example.com', 'https://staging.example.com']` not wildcard
- Validate the `Origin` header against your allowlist on every request — don't reflect arbitrary origins
- Restrict `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` to only the HTTP methods your API actually uses — `GET, POST, PUT, DELETE`
- Limit `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` to headers your API expects — `Content-Type, Authorization` not wildcard
- Set `Access-Control-Max-Age` to cache preflight responses — `86400` (24 hours) reduces OPTIONS request overhead
- Use `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only when your API needs cookies or auth headers from the browser
- Never expose sensitive headers — configure `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` to only include headers the frontend needs
- Handle preflight OPTIONS requests explicitly — return 204 with CORS headers, no body
- Use different CORS configs per environment — development can be permissive, production must be strict
- Log rejected CORS requests — they may indicate misconfigured frontends or attack attempts
- Test CORS configuration with `curl -H 'Origin: https://evil.com'` — verify your server rejects unauthorized origins
